newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares fall 1.64 pct on rating rumour.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares fall 1.64 pct on rating rumour.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell an average 1.64 percent on Friday amid rumours that Moody's may downgrade Turkey's rating soon and caution ahead of next week's censure motion vote threatening the government, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed 27 points lower at 1,615, after brushing a high of 1,656 in early trade.
Daily volume was little changed at 30.42 trillion lira after Thursday's 30.2 trillion.
"The market mainly used rumours that Moody's might soon downgrade Turkey's rating as an excuse for the drop," said Nermin Samiloglu from Tacirler securities.
She said selling in the afternoon was led by state-owned shares which have major impact on the index, after the index closed up two points in the morning session.
The index gained 3.86 percent over the week due to a 5.7 percent jump in the past three days caused by easing political concerns.
The market was relieved after parliament rejected sending Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller to the Supreme Court in three corruption charge votes this week.
Brokers expect caution to continue early next week. Parliament will on Tuesday debate a censure motion filed by leftist parties against the Islamist-led coalition government.
Conservative opposition party ANAP said it would submit a separate censure motion on Monday.

Of the 238 shares traded, losers outdid rises by 157 to 42 and 39 closed steady. The IMKB Industrial fell 1.07 percent to 1,660, the IMKB Services lost 1.87 percent to 1,472 and the IMKB Financial shed 1.88 percent to 1,672.

Actives were led by largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, up 250 lira at 21,500, utility Cukurova Elektrik, down 5,000 lira at 212,500 and T.Isbank's C series shares which fell 1,500 lira to 40,500.
They made up 26.7 percent of the total volume.
